slides.title: KV Resume on WSE-3
slides.subtitle: Measured costs of recompute, reload, and resident-prefix prefill.
slides.notes: The question is not which lane is universally best. It is which cost dominates under a specific resume state and implementation.

slides.title: Experiment topology: prefill card → hosts → decode card
slides.caption: Each kernel uses a 2×4 serpentine pipeline of 256×256-PE blocks. Prefill gathers KV east into kv_mux and drains north; decode accepts the host KV stream through adaptor + kv_demux and shifts column slices north into the fabric.
slides.notes: This is the logical topology used by the measured pdSeparate implementation, not a to-scale wafer map. The cards do not share an on-wafer relay seam: KV crosses through their separate host memories. The layer slices across B0…B7 are 2,4,4,4,4,4,4,2.

slides.title: Three request paths on the same simplified topology
slides.caption: A sends token IDs to decode and rebuilds all KV; B reloads persisted history KV and computes only Lnew; C extends resident KV on prefill, then transfers the completed state through both hosts.
slides.notes: One PE represents the complete 2×4 kernel fabric from slide 2. Each row uses one prefill card and one decode card with separate host memory. The dashed host-to-host leg in C is assumed zero in the current latency model.

slides.title: Three ways to resume an evicted request

left.heading: History, delta, generation
left.body: PD separation: prefill and decode each occupy one WSE card with separate host DRAM. Lhist KV is assumed persisted; Lnew has no KV. We time resume only—decode→host eviction and host-to-host latency are excluded.

highlights: A — force-decode Lhist + Lnew in decode; no reload
B — reload Lhist KV; force-decode only Lnew
C — prefill Lnew over resident Lhist; transfer the completed KV state to decode
slides.notes: Lane B assumes the history was already persisted. E13, the decode egress half, is not implemented, so this is not yet a round-trip eviction policy.

slides.title: The experiments do not all exercise the same kernel path
slides.notes: All reported device spans use the 0.85 GHz TSC conversion. Failed EPCC 502 repeats and a run without a downloaded hash-verified evidence bundle are excluded.

slides.title: All 24 force-decode spans across prefix × forced length
slides.caption: RAW — P={256,1024,4096,8192}, F={1,256,512,1024,2048,4096}; real Qwen3-1.7B on WSE-3, n=1.
slides.notes: The large separation at small F is visible before any offset subtraction or regression.

slides.title: Startup anchor + position-dependent intervals
slides.caption: D(P,F)=D(P,256)+Σ II(q), where 16 steady segments give II(q)=71.745 µs+4.093 ns·q. Ready/fill/tail are inferred.
slides.notes: The source-level timer starts after a locally-ready west-edge sender emits [N,F], before HT_tail receives first Z. It is not an all-PE readiness barrier. Exact attribution needs a first-Z timestamp.

slides.title: Complete force-decode equations
slides.caption: The discrete sum and closed form are equivalent. D(P,256) is interpolated between measured prefix anchors; F=1 is not subtracted as a universal offset.
slides.notes: The closed form follows from summing q from P+256 through P+F−1: there are F−256 terms and their sum is (F−256)(2P+F+255)/2.

slides.title: Decode KV ingress: six raw measurements
slides.caption: RAW — six device-TSC observations on the pdSeparate ingress path, spanning the floor, knee, and byte-dominated region.
slides.notes: Do not compare this bandwidth directly with E6 prefill egress: E6 performs a transpose and switch-gather in addition to moving bytes.

slides.title: Reload = floor + payload term
slides.caption: I(H) uses piecewise-linear interpolation of the six E5 anchors; the saturated region approaches 3.186 GB/s aggregate.
slides.notes: The A/B boundary calculation uses the measured-anchor interpolation, not a single bandwidth number across the whole payload range.

slides.title: Lane B reload equations
slides.caption: Delta reload pays I(H); full-context reload pays I(S+H). Both then force-decode Lnew using the Lane A model at absolute prefix S+H.
slides.notes: I(h) is piecewise-linear interpolation over the six E5 anchors. E10 validates that the real reload path reproduces E5 and that post-ingress forced-token cost matches E9 to 0.97–1.00 across H=512…8192.

slides.title: The measured flip and the projected crossing
slides.caption: Left: E10D offset-controlled totals. Right: E14+E5 observed-span projection gives H*=744 (S=256, Lnew=256, delta reload); compare winner/crossing, not absolute y-values.
slides.notes: The left panel is the E10D offset-controlled direct comparison. The right panel is the newer E14 observed-span model, so the absolute y-values should not be overlaid; the robust shared conclusion is the winner flip and a crossing between the two direct witnesses. Other starting prefixes and full-context reload move the projected boundary.

slides.title: Two resident-prefix prefill cases at total context 8,192
slides.caption: MEASURED + DERIVED — direct S6a prefill compute at total context 8,192; forced and lane totals combine E9/E5/E6 evidence.
slides.notes: The two resident-prefix compute measurements were byte-identical across cold/warm and warm/warm checks. Exact pdSeparate lacks START_CHUNKS, so this is a validated screening result, not the final pdSeparate benchmark.

slides.title: A conditional policy, with explicit gaps
rows: Forced steady cost grows with position
Crossing moves with S and reload policy
Full eviction round trip favors B
slides.notes: The safe conclusion is a workload- and implementation-dependent segmented policy, not a universal 700-token rule.

slides.title: Only run experiments that can change the decision
